title: Vintage Gibson Acoustic Value Guide: Models And Prices
description: Compare vintage Gibson acoustic value references for J-45, J-200, Hummingbird and LG models, with condition context and photographs from my own archive.

alt: Sunburst J-45 with a large mottled pickguard lying in a brown case

faqs.q: How Do I Find The Value Of My Gibson Acoustic Guitar?
faqs.a: Start with the exact model, then match the year, configuration and condition. I can begin an individual appraisal with clear photographs and the history you know.

faqs.q: Are All These Prices Based On The Same Condition?
faqs.a: The guide-value ranges assume clean originals with their original cases. Wear, replacement parts and structural repairs need to be assessed before comparing an individual guitar.

faqs.q: Why Do Some Years Share A Price Range?
faqs.a: Adjacent years can share an era range. The annual row helps you find the year, but condition and configuration still determine the appraisal.

faqs.q: Can I Use A Current Listing As A Completed Price?
faqs.a: No. An advertised amount is an asking price, and a sold label doesn't always disclose the final negotiated amount. The final selling price can differ from the advertised amount.

faqs.q: Does A Quality Refret Remove All-Original Status?
faqs.a: A quality refret preserves the all-original classification of an otherwise original instrument while removing museum-quality status. Refinishing, neck reshaping and structural repairs are separate changes.
